newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian bank bad loans rise in June - ABI.
newsitem.headline: Italian bank bad loans rise in June - ABI.

text.p: Italian banks' gross bad loans in June rose 15.8 percent to 116.76 trillion lire from the same month last year, the Italian Banking Association (ABI) said in its latest monthly report.
Bad loans in May totalled 115.42 trillion lire, a 15.4 percent rise on May 1995.
The ratio of bad loans to total loans, on a gross basis, rose to 10.88 percent from 10.86 percent.
ABI, giving details of bank loans for September, said that for banks with short-term deposits total loans increased 3.66 percent on September 1995 to 856.0 trillion lire.
In August, loans rose 3.57 percent to 856.5 trillion.
Lira loans rose 6.24 percent to 779.0 trillion lire while foreign currency denominated loans fell 16.78 percent to 77.0 trillion lire.
For the entire banking system, for which only data to end-August were available, ABI said total loans amounted to 1,062 trillion lire, 1.9 percent up on August last year.
